title: The Kabbalah Unveiled
author: S. L. MacGregor Mathers (trans)
description: The Kabbalah Unveiled (Kabbala Denudata), translated into English by S. L. MacGregor Mathers (London, 1887) from the Latin of Christian Knorr von Rosenroth's Kabbala Denudata (1677-84), with an introduction by Mathers. It contains three key books of the Zohar: the Book of Concealed Mystery (Sifra di-Tzeniuta), the Greater Holy Assembly (Idra Rabba) and the Lesser Holy Assembly (Idra Zuta). These describe in daring anthropomorphic imagery the emanation of the divine 'countenances': the Ancient of Days or Vast Countenance (Arikh Anpin) and the Lesser Countenance (Zeir Anpin), their heads, beards and features, and the balancing of mercy and severity in the structure of the sefirot. Mathers, a founder of the Golden Dawn, introduced the Kabbalah to the English occult revival through this work, which became a foundational text for Hermetic Qabalah.
